days.title: Ho Chi Minh City · arrival, Post Office + Nguyen Hue

cost.note: Deluxe double, typical Oct rate (~US$145); a bit over the US$50 pp/night Vietnam lodging line

stay.note: Check-in 14:00 — you arrive ~15:00. Ask for a high floor facing the Opera House.

days.dayNote:
- Clocks went back 2 h on landing (KST → ICT, UTC+7).
- SGN T2 immigration with the e-visa: allow 30–60 min; get VND from an airport ATM (a few million) and a local SIM/eSIM.
- **Grab** (car) is the default way around Vietnam — install it and add a card before the trip.
- Saigon **Notre-Dame Cathedral** (next to the Post Office) is still under restoration — completion has slipped to 2027 or later, so expect scaffolding and no interior.
- Addresses: HCMC abolished its districts in 2025 (wards now), but everyone still says "District 1".

leg.label: Grab · SGN T2 → District 1
leg.note: Grab pickup zone outside arrivals; 30–45 min depending on traffic.

items.title: Late lunch · bánh mì or phở near the hotel
items.note: Snack-sized — dinner is at 19:00. Ideas: Bánh Mì Huỳnh Hoa (26 Lê Thị Riêng, huge and famous; its hours have changed over the years, check first) or any phở shop around Ben Thanh.

items.node: Vietnam|Ho Chi Minh City||Saigon Central Post Office
items.note: ~07:00–19:00 daily (verify). 1880s French post office with the vaulted hall and painted maps; still sells stamps + postcards. **Book Street** (Nguyễn Văn Bình) runs alongside; Notre-Dame is across the square (exterior only, restoration).

items.node: Vietnam|Ho Chi Minh City||Nguyen Hue Walking Street
items.note: Start at the People's Committee building (exterior, lit at night) and walk toward the river. The Café Apartments (42 Nguyễn Huệ) has cafés on every floor — pick one with a balcony.

items.node: Vietnam|Ho Chi Minh City||Saigon Saigon Rooftop Bar

items.note: Sunset ~17:35. 10th floor of your hotel; smart-casual.

items.title: Dinner · Bánh Xèo 46A
items.note: Order bánh xèo + gỏi cuốn (fresh rolls): wrap pieces of the crêpe in mustard greens and herbs, dip in nước chấm. Open-air, cash. ~10 min by Grab.

days.title: Ho Chi Minh City · Cu Chi Tunnels + Bui Vien
days.dayNote:
- **Cu Chi:** go early — it's hot and tour buses arrive from ~10:00. Wear clothes that can get dirty and closed shoes; the crawl sections are optional.
- Alternative transport: a speedboat Cu Chi tour up the Saigon River (e.g. Les Rives) instead of the car — pricier, more scenic.
- **War Remnants Museum** is heavy going (Agent Orange, photo-journalist rooms) — pace yourselves.
- XO Tours ends ~22:00; ask to be dropped at Bui Vien. Rain plan: afternoon showers are common — the museum and the tour run in the rain (ponchos provided).

leg.label: Private car · District 1 → Cu Chi (Ben Dinh)

cost.note: Round trip with the driver waiting (~6 h); hotel car or a Klook/GetYourGuide private transfer

days.title: Ho Chi Minh City · Independence Palace, Ben Thanh + food
days.dayNote:
- Morning cluster in Tân Định (phở → pink church → Jade Emperor), then the palace and Ben Thanh; rest through the midday heat.
- **Tax refund with passport:** Vietnam's VAT refund works only with a VAT-refund invoice from a participating store (≥ VND 2 million per store per day), goods unused, claimed at the departure airport — for this trip at **HAN T2 on Nov 2**. Markets (Ben Thanh) and tailors don't issue these.
- Friday night: Bui Vien is at its loudest if you want round two; Chill Skybar (AB Tower, Lê Lai) is the dressy rooftop alternative.

cost.note: Deluxe river/pool view, typical Oct rate (~US$110)

stay.note: Check-in ~16:20. The Da Nang block (3 days) is based here: tailor fittings + Old Town evenings; Da Nang sights are day trips.

days.dayNote:
- Domestic flights leave from **SGN Terminal 3**; VN132 fare must include checked bags.
- ⚠ Late October is central Vietnam's rainiest month (flooding in the Old Town some years; typhoon risk): pack a light rain jacket, check the forecast daily, and keep the tailor schedule fixed while swapping sightseeing days around it.
- Hoi An has been part of Da Nang city since 2025 (addresses may say "Đà Nẵng").
- Dragon Bridge show is planned for Sun night (Oct 24), not tonight.

items.title: Check in · Little Riverside Hoi An
Tailor quote · Yaly Couture
items.note: Priciest, mixed reviews (shopping list) — use it as the price/quality benchmark. Get a written quote per piece.

items.title: Tailor quote · A Dong Silk
items.note: Second quote; compare fabrics side by side (take photos of the swatches + prices).

items.title: Order the tailoring · BeBe Tailor (or the best quote)
items.note:
**Order everything today** (day 1 of the Hoi An block) so there's time for 2+ fittings.
- Dennis: suit. Both: overcoat, trench coat. Audrey: ao dai. Optional: leather wallet (Dennis) / bag (Audrey) — Hoi An leather shops make them in 1–2 days.
- Bring reference photos; **see and feel the cloth** and ask what the wool actually is (pure wool vs. blend). Rough suit prices: ~$80–150 basic, $180–300 mid-range, $280–500 good wool (shopping list).
- Get written quotes at 2–3 shops (Yaly and A Dong Silk before this), then order at the best — BeBe is the default; Ba Ri and 45 Thu are the other names that come up.
- Agree the fittings now: **Sun 15:30, Mon 17:30, final Tue 08:30**; pay a 30–50% deposit; get a receipt listing each piece, fabric and price; ask about shipping anything unfinished to Hanoi.

items.title: Dinner · Morning Glory
items.note: Hoi An classics: cao lầu, white rose dumplings, mì Quảng, bánh xèo. Busy on Saturdays — go by ~19:45 or book.

items.note: Across the An Hội bridge; lantern stalls and riverside lights. The lantern boat is planned for Mon.

days.title: Hoi An · My Son, Old Town + Dragon Bridge
days.dayNote:
- Long day (05:30 → ~22:15), with a pool break at midday.
- **Rain plan:** swap with Mon (Ba Na) if today is the drier day — My Son and the Old Town are fine in light rain; the fitting stays at 15:30.
- The **Old Town ticket** (~120k VND pp, 5 coupons) covers the Covered Bridge, Fujian Hall, Quan Cong Temple + 2 more (e.g. Tan Ky Old House, a museum). Buy at any ticket booth; keep it for evening walks.
- Dragon Bridge: fire & water show at **21:00** Sat/Sun (2026 local listings say Fri–Sun); cancelled in storms.

items.title: Breakfast · hotel breakfast box
items.note: Ask reception the evening before (buffet usually opens ~06:30).

items.note: Pick seafood from the tanks — **confirm the price per kg before it's cooked**. Try scallops with scallion oil, clams in lemongrass broth, grilled squid, a whole fish.

items.title: Dragon Bridge fire & water show
items.note: Show at **21:00**, ~15–20 min: fire bursts first, then water. Stand on the east bank near the dragon's head (Trần Hưng Đạo / Võ Văn Kiệt) or on the bridge's side walkways — the front rows get soaked. Car back to Hoi An ~50 min.

days.title: Da Nang · Ba Na Hills + Marble Mountains
days.dayNote:
- Ba Na on a **Monday** = fewer domestic weekend crowds than Sunday.
- ⚠ **Weather:** Ba Na's summit (~1,400 m) is often in cloud in late October. Check the forecast / Sun World webcam at 07:00: if socked in, skip Ba Na and do Marble Mountains + the Museum of Cham Sculpture (Da Nang) + An Bang beach instead.
- Summit is ~8–10 °C cooler than Hoi An — bring a layer and a rain jacket.

cost.note: Day hire: Ba Na → Marble Mountains → Hoi An

items.note: Head here first off the cable car (Included in the Ba Na Hills ticket — places note), before the crowds and before clouds build.

cost.note: Adult ticket incl. cable cars — 2026 estimate ~900k–1M VND; buy online on the Sun World site/app; buffet lunch extra

items.note: Cable cars ~07:30/08:00–17:00 (verify). French Village, Le Jardin d'Amour gardens, Linh Ứng pagoda on the peak, Fantasy Park (indoor, good if it rains). Record-length cable car ride (~20 min).

items.title: Lunch · Ba Na Hills
items.note: Buffet at the French Village (combo ticket) or the Beer Plaza; pricier than town.

leg.label: Private car · Ba Na Hills → Marble Mountains

items.note: ~07:00–17:30. Climb Thủy Sơn: Huyền Không cave (light shafts, shrine), Tam Thai + Linh Ứng pagodas, Vọng Giang viewpoint. Lots of steps (elevator one way). The stone-carving shops at the base push hard — browse only.

leg.label: Private car · Marble Mountains → Hoi An

items.note: Second fitting (near-final). Try every piece with the shoes/shirt you'll wear. Confirm the final pickup **Tue 08:30** and shipping to the Hanoi hotel for anything that can't be finished.

items.note: Ideas: Bale Well (Giếng Bá Lễ, 45/51 Trần Hưng Đạo — one set menu of bánh xèo, nem lụi and rice paper rolls), or riverside places on Bạch Đằng.

- Son Tra detour runs from ~10:30 to 14:00; skip it and go to An Bang beach instead if it's pouring.
- VN174 fare should include checked bags (tailoring adds weight; buy extra kg online if needed).

items.title: Final fitting + pickup · BeBe Tailor
items.note: Check seams, lining, buttons, sleeve + trouser lengths, how the coats sit over a jacket. Pay the balance (cash avoids a ~3% card fee). Ask for garment bags.

items.title: Son Tra peninsula · look for douc langurs
items.note: **MONKEYS!!!** (places note). Red-shanked douc langurs live in the canopy along the Son Tra roads; best odds early morning or late afternoon, midday is hit-or-miss — ask the driver to stop at the known langur spots and scan the treetops quietly. Don't feed the macaques (they grab bags).
Linh Ứng Pagoda: the 67 m Lady Buddha facing the bay; free. Cover shoulders and knees.

items.note: Ask the hotel; goat hotpot or river fish.

stay.note: Arrive ~07:15. Standard check-in is 14:00 — guarantee an immediate room by booking from the night of Oct 28 (+1 night, ~2.6M VND), or at least request early check-in + store bags and shower.

days.dayNote:
- Late October is one of Sa Pa's best months: dry, clear-ish, post-harvest terraces. Days 15–20 °C, nights ~12 °C.
- **Fansipan first** — mornings are clearer; clouds build after noon. If the summit is in cloud at 08:00 (check the Sun World webcam), swap Fansipan and Cat Cat, or skip Fansipan.
- You slept on a train: the 90-min rest after lunch is deliberate.

items.note: ~20-min cable car up to ~3,000 m, then ~600 steps (or the tram) to the 3,143 m summit marker; pagodas and a giant Buddha on the ridge. **Cold and windy on top** — bring the warm layers. Last cars down ~17:00.

items.title: Dinner · Sa Pa town
items.note: Sa Pa specialties: salmon/sturgeon hotpot (lẩu cá hồi), street-grill BBQ skewers, thắng cố (adventurous). Walk the Stone Church square and the night market after.

days.dayNote:

- **Saturday-night train sells out** — the SP4 cabin must be booked early (see todo). Pick up snacks + water in town.

notes: File name: SCHEMA.md and allocation.json call this part `days-vietnam.json`; the task text said `vietnam.json`. Written as days-vietnam.json, with vietnam.json as a symlink to it (same as the Korea/Taiwan builders).

Night trains: the allocation's SP1 21:35→05:15 / SP2 20:55→04:35 don't appear in every 2026 timetable; 2026 sources consistently list SP3 (Hanoi 22:00 → Lao Cai ~05:55–06:05) and SP4 (Lao Cai 21:30 → Hanoi ~05:25–05:35) as the daily trains carrying the private cabin carriages (Chapa Express etc.). Drafted with SP3/SP4 (22:00→06:00, 21:30→05:30). Sleep kinds/dates unchanged; the Hanoi hotel is still booked from Oct 30 for the ~05:45 arrival. Re-check the 2027 timetable and the Hanoi boarding gate (main station, 120 Lê Duẩn, vs the Trần Quý Cáp side) when booking.

Priorities: all Vietnam places in the Places tab are unrated, so the order follows the Cities-tab notes + places notes (Ben Thanh, Cu Chi, Bui Vien, Post Office; Ba Na/Golden Bridge, Monkey Mountain ('MONKEYS!!!'), Marble Mountain, My Son, Lady Buddha, Dragon Bridge, My Khe; Old Town + its 3 sights; Old Quarter, Train Street, Beer Street; Mua Caves, Trang An, Tam Coc; Sa Pa) plus judgment. Every listed Vietnam place is scheduled once. New unrated classics added as nodes (Independence Palace, War Remnants Museum, Jade Emperor Pagoda, HCMC Museum, Hoan Kiem Lake, Ngoc Son, Hoa Lo, Temple of Literature, One Pillar Pagoda, water puppets, Hoa Lu, Cat Cat, Fansipan, Muong Hoa trek) without priorities.

Da Nang/Hoi An order differs from the allocation's suggestion: Sun Oct 24 = My Son early + Old Town + the Dragon Bridge show (21:00 Sat/Sun; 2026 local listings say Fri–Sun); Mon Oct 25 = Ba Na Hills (weekday crowds) + Marble Mountains; Tue Oct 26 = Son Tra (langurs, Lady Buddha) on the way to DAD. Tailoring: ordered Sat ~18:00, fittings Sun 15:30, Mon 17:30, final Tue 08:30.

Ninh Binh: the task asked for early Trang An boats, so Trang An is Thu Oct 28 at 07:00 (first boats) and Tam Coc is the Wed Oct 27 afternoon boat; Mua Caves at sunset Oct 27. The allocation had these the other way round.

Weather risk: late October is peak rain/flood/typhoon season in central Vietnam (Hoi An Old Town floods some years; Ba Na's summit is often in cloud) — dayNotes give swaps. HCMC is at the end of its rainy season; Hanoi, Ninh Binh and Sa Pa are dry and mild (Fansipan summit ~0–10 °C).

Hotels are draft picks (existence + pins checked on OpenStreetMap): Caravelle Saigon, Little Riverside Hoi An, La Siesta Premium Hàng Bè, Tam Coc Garden Resort, Pao's Sapa Leisure Hotel. Nightly prices are typical October rates from memory (not quotes). Vietnam lodging averages ~US$55 pp/night vs the US$50 line.
Hanoi stays: Oct 26 (1 night) + Oct 31 block (2 nights) as stays; the paid early night of Oct 30 is an explicit lodging expense on the hotel node (Oct 30 is a train night, stay = null).

Prices: VND at ~26,000/USD, 2025–26 levels. Verified on 2026-09-23: Independence Palace hours + 80k combo (official site); Dragon Bridge show 21:00 weekends; SP3/SP4 times (several ticket sites); Notre-Dame Saigon still under restoration. Marked '(verify)': most restaurant hours, My Son opening (06:00 vs 06:30), Ba Na (~950k), Fansipan (~800k), Cu Chi (125k), Hoi An Old Town (120k), Temple of Literature (70k), Ngoc Son, Tam Coc, Mua, Cat Cat, water-puppet show times.

Pins: every new node was looked up on OpenStreetMap/Nominatim (2026-09-23); confidence 'high' = matching OSM object at that address. Medium: BeBe Tailor (OSM has 'Bebe Clothing' at 05–07 Hoàng Diệu), Pao's Sapa (OSM street name differs), Nguyen Hue Walking Street (mid-boulevard), Muong Hoa Valley (between Lao Chai and Ta Van). Lao Cai Station is filed under Sa Pa (no Lao Cai city in the Cities tab).

Administrative changes (2025): HCMC's districts were replaced by wards (addresses use the new ward names; 'District 1' kept informally); Hoi An is now inside Da Nang city; Sa Pa is a ward of the enlarged Lao Cai province. Node cities follow the Cities tab (Hoi An, Sa Pa kept).

Restaurants named only where well known and confirmed on OSM (Bánh Xèo 46A, Phở Hòa Pasteur, Cục Gạch Quán, Morning Glory, Madam Khánh, Bé Mặn, Mì Quảng 1A, Phở Bát Đàn, Bánh Mì 25, Café Giảng, Bún Chả Hương Liên, Chả Cá Thăng Long, Tầm Vị, The Hill Station); other meals are title-only with ideas in the note.

Day capacity: every day's item time (incl. meals and rests) is ≤ 750 min; the heaviest are Oct 21 (735) and Oct 31 (740, incl. a 3 h sleep after the night train). Oct 24 runs 05:30–22:15 with a 90-min midday rest.
